The Stool of the Ujah: Sacred Kingship and Elder Governance

By Dr. Joshua M. Garba

The traditional monarchy of the Anaguta Kingdom—embodied in the paramount stool of the Ujah—is one of the oldest institutions of sovereign governance on the Jos Plateau.

Dual Authority: Monarch and Elders

The governance structure of the Anaguta is characterized by a balance of power. While the Ujah serves as supreme spiritual custodian and political representative of the kingdom, major decisions are reached in consensus with the Council of Elders (representing the twelve foundational clans).

Coronation Rites

Ascension to the throne involves intricate purification ceremonies held at secluded ancestral groves. The incoming sovereign is handed the ancient staff of acacia wood, the sacred quiver, and the royal leopard skin mantle, swearing to govern with compassion, truth, and unwavering protection of the land.

Modern Cultural Stewardship

Under the reign of His Royal Majesty Pozoh Johnson Jauro Magaji, the royal palace has become a modern center for educational scholarships, conflict resolution, inter-ethnic harmony, and cultural research programs.
